score_rationale: Strong commercial validation with established database vendors actively selling franchisee and franchise owner contact lists: Franchimp (450,000+ franchisees across database with ability to filter by franchise name and ownership type: franchisee-owned vs. company-owned), Franchisee List / FranchiseeList.com (brand-specific lists including Subway franchisee contact list with emails, phones, addresses, names for 20,000+ franchised Subway sandwich shop locations in USA, and McDonald's franchisee list with contact details for 14,000+ McDonald's locations mostly franchisee-owned), Data Man Group (franchise owners marketing lists), and FranchiseComplaints.org (publicly accessible Subway franchise owners contact list with personal phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses). Over 1.5 million franchise businesses available in U.S. per Franchimp data. Four high-value B2B buyer segments with strong LTV justification: (1) Point-of-sale (POS) and restaurant management software vendors (Toast POS serving 120,000+ restaurants including many franchisees at $69-$165/month base software plus $0.15 + 2.49% per transaction generating $800-$2,000/month all-in cost for busy franchise location processing $100K-$500K/month = $10,000-$24,000/year per location, Square for Restaurants at $60/month + processing fees, Clover POS at $14.95-$799.95/month + 2.3% + $0.10 per transaction, Lightspeed Restaurant POS, Revel Systems, SpotOn, Aloha NCR) selling mission-critical systems where franchisee customers running 1-10 locations pay $10,000-$240,000/year and customer lifetime value over 8-12 year retention reaches $80,000-$2,880,000 for multi-unit operators, making $149-$199 database deliver 400×-14,000× ROI when just two multi-unit franchisees are closed; (2) Payroll, HR, and employee management software vendors (Gusto payroll and benefits for small businesses at $40/month + $6/employee serving franchisees with 5-50 employees = $70-$340/month = $840-$4,080/year, ADP Workforce Now for franchise enterprises at $100-$200/month base + per-employee fees for 20-200 employee multi-unit operators = $2,000-$10,000/year, Paychex, OnPay, Rippling, Homebase employee scheduling and time tracking at $20-$100/month, 7shifts restaurant scheduling, When I Work) where one multi-unit franchisee = 4×-50× database cost annually and 40×-500× over 10-year relationship; (3) Commercial insurance brokers specializing in franchise business (general liability, property, workers' comp, business interruption, product liability for restaurants/retail with annual premiums $15,000-$150,000 for single-location franchisees scaling to $150,000-$1,500,000 for multi-unit operators owning 10-100 locations, generating $3,000-$300,000 in annual broker commissions at 20% typical, with specialized franchise insurance programs from Insureon, CoverWallet, Next Insurance, The Hartford, Travelers) where one multi-unit franchisee client = 15×-1,500× database cost annually; (4) Equipment suppliers, commercial kitchen vendors, and facilities maintenance providers (commercial refrigeration repair and replacement for restaurants at $5,000-$50,000 per location, POS hardware and payment terminals, commercial ovens/fryers/grills for QSR franchises at $20,000-$100,000 kitchen remodel per location × 5-10 locations = $100,000-$1,000,000 multi-unit upgrade cycles, HVAC maintenance contracts for retail/restaurant spaces, signage and branding materials per franchisor specifications, commercial cleaning and janitorial services at $500-$5,000/month per location, hood cleaning and fire suppression for restaurant kitchens) where one multi-unit equipment sale or maintenance contract = 250×-5,000× database ROI. Total addressable market: Franchimp reports 1.5M+ franchise businesses in U.S. (includes both franchisee-owned and company-owned locations, need to filter for franchisee-owned only), with top franchise brands including McDonald's 14,000+ U.S. locations mostly franchisee-owned (McDonald's corporate owns <5% of locations, 95%+ franchised per company policy requiring franchisee operators), Subway 20,000+ franchised locations in USA (down from peak 27,000 due to closures but still largest restaurant chain by unit count), 7-Eleven, Dunkin', Taco Bell, Burger King, Wendy's, Sonic, Domino's Pizza, Papa John's, Little Caesars, Popeyes, Chick-fil-A (unique model: company-owned real estate but operator franchisees), Arby's, Jimmy John's, Dairy Queen, Baskin-Robbins, Great Clips, Sport Clips, Anytime Fitness, Planet Fitness, The UPS Store, Jersey Mike's Subs, Firehouse Subs, Five Guys, Wingstop, Buffalo Wild Wings, MOD Pizza, Moe's Southwest Grill, Qdoba, Panda Express, Chipotle (company-owned, not franchised — exclude), Panera Bread, Starbucks (company-owned, not franchised — exclude). Estimated 300,000-500,000 individual franchisee owner contacts (many franchisees own multiple units: average McDonald's franchisee owns 6-8 locations per IFA data, Subway franchisees often own 2-5 locations, creating ~20,000-30,000 Subway franchisee owners managing 20,000+ locations, and ~2,000-3,000 McDonald's franchisee owners managing 14,000 locations), concentrated in QSR (quick-service restaurants: burgers, pizza, sandwiches, coffee, chicken), fast casual (Chipotle, Panera, MOD Pizza), fitness franchises (Anytime Fitness 5,000+ franchisee-owned clubs, Planet Fitness, Orangetheory, F45, Pure Barre), automotive services (Jiffy Lube, Meineke, Midas, AAMCO transmission, Christian Brothers Automotive), personal services (Great Clips 4,400+ salons, Sport Clips, Supercuts, massage franchises, tanning salons), home services (Mosquito Joe, Window Genie, Molly Maid, TWO MEN AND A TRUCK, Mr. Rooter Plumbing, Aire Serv HVAC, Mr. Electric, Glass Doctor), business services (The UPS Store 5,000+ locations, FedEx Office, PostNet, Minuteman Press printing), education and child development (Kumon, Mathnasium, The Goddard School, Primrose Schools), senior care (Home Instead, Visiting Angels, Right at Home), and specialty retail (7-Eleven 13,000+ franchised convenience stores, GNC nutrition, Batteries Plus Bulbs, Pet Supplies Plus). Public data availability is PARTIAL: Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDD) filed with state regulators (14 states require FDD registration: California, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, New York, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin per FTC Franchise Rule) contain Item 20 exhibit listing all current franchisees with contact information, however FDDs are not always publicly downloadable (some states charge $25-$100 per FDD copy, others require FOIA requests, California provides online search but charges for documents). Secretary of State business registrations contain franchise business entities (DBAs like 'McDonald's Restaurant #12345 - John Smith Owner' or 'Subway Sandwich Shop - Jane Doe'), but linking these to parent franchise brand and identifying owner contact info requires significant data engineering. Alternative approach: scrape franchise location finder websites (McDonald's location finder shows all 14,000+ restaurants with addresses, Subway restaurant locator, Dunkin' store locator) to get location addresses, then cross-reference with county business license databases and Secretary of State records to identify franchisee owner names and mailing addresses, enrich with email/phone via business directory lookups. Engineering lift is moderate-to-high: (a) obtain FDDs from 14 registration states for top 100-500 franchise brands (estimated 500-2,000 FDD documents at $0-$100 each = $0-$200K total cost if purchasing all, or focus on free states California/Minnesota/Wisconsin online databases), (b) parse Item 20 franchisee exhibit tables (usually PDF format with inconsistent schemas: some list names/addresses in table format, others narrative text, requiring OCR + AI extraction), (c) scrape franchise location finders for 100+ major brands to compile master location database (200,000-500,000 total franchise locations across top brands), (d) cross-reference location addresses with Secretary of State business entity databases in all 50 states to find registered owner names (search for DBAs containing franchise brand name + location identifiers), (e) enrich owner contact info via ZoomInfo/Apollo for multi-unit operators (often have LLC management companies), LinkedIn for individual franchisees, county business license databases for mailing addresses, (f) deduplicate multi-unit owners appearing in multiple location records, (g) classify by franchise brand, industry vertical (QSR, fitness, automotive, personal services, etc.), unit count per owner (single-unit vs. multi-unit operator), and estimated annual revenue tier. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad — Franchimp and Franchisee List vendors use login-required platforms or brand-specific list sales (Subway list, McDonald's list sold separately) with enterprise quote-required pricing, typical B2B patterns of $0.25-$0.75 per contact for franchise owner data (higher pricing than generic business lists due to niche audience and data collection difficulty) = $12,500-$37,500 for 50,000-record list. Score is 7 (not 8) due to: (a) moderate commercial validation with 3-4 vendors (Franchimp, Franchisee List, Data Man Group, FranchiseComplaints.org) vs. 6-7 vendors for higher-scoring opportunities, (b) high buyer LTV across all four segments (POS software $80K-$2.88M lifetime for multi-unit operators, payroll/HR $8K-$100K over 10 years, insurance $3K-$300K annual commissions, equipment/services $5K-$1M per multi-unit contract) where 1-2 customer acquisitions justify 400×-14,000× database investment creating strong willingness-to-pay, (c) moderate TAM size (300K-500K franchisee owners vs. 800K-1M insurance agents or 400K-600K property managers, but highly concentrated in high-value multi-unit operators: top 20% of franchisees own 5-50 units each representing 70-80% of total revenue per IFA data, creating quality-over-quantity opportunity), (d) partial public data availability with moderate-to-high engineering complexity (FDDs available in 14 states but require purchase/FOIA in many cases, Item 20 exhibits lack standardized format requiring AI parsing, no centralized national franchisee registry, must cross-reference location scrapers with SOS business records and business licenses across 50 states to identify owners), (e) alternative data sources exist but require extensive aggregation and enrichment (franchise location finders provide addresses but not owners, SOS business registrations contain some franchise DBAs but inconsistent naming, county business licenses vary by jurisdiction), and (f) clear buyer pain points validated by commercial market (POS vendors must reach franchisees before franchisor-mandated tech upgrades, insurance brokers target franchise verticals with specialized coverage needs, payroll vendors pursue multi-unit operators needing enterprise HR systems, equipment suppliers chase kitchen remodel and branding cycles). Score not higher than 7 due to fragmented data sources (no single authoritative public database like IRS 990s or state insurance licensing, requiring multi-step compilation from FDDs + location scrapers + SOS records) and partial paywall barriers (some state FDD access requires $25-$100 per document purchase vs. free bulk downloads for higher-scoring opportunities), though commercial demand is strong (franchise owners are known high-value B2B buyers with captive need for POS, payroll, insurance, equipment creating sustained vendor interest).
summary: A comprehensive CSV of all identifiable U.S. franchisee owners and multi-unit franchise operators extracted from state-registered Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDD) Item 20 exhibits (14 registration states), franchise brand location finders cross-referenced with Secretary of State business entity databases, and county business license records. Each record includes franchisee owner name (individual or LLC management company), franchise brand (McDonald's, Subway, Dunkin', 7-Eleven, Anytime Fitness, The UPS Store, etc.), unit count per owner (single-unit operator vs. multi-unit owner managing 2-50 locations), location addresses for owned units, corporate/home mailing address, phone, email (enriched via business directories), industry vertical (QSR quick-service restaurant, fast casual, fitness, automotive services, personal services, home services, business services, senior care, education, specialty retail), estimated annual revenue tier (infer from unit count × average unit volume: $500K-$3M per QSR location, $200K-$1M per fitness franchise, $300K-$800K per personal services), and years in franchise system (where disclosed in FDD exhibits). As of 2026, Franchimp reports 1.5M+ franchise businesses in U.S. (mix of franchisee-owned and company-owned locations), with major brands including McDonald's 14,000+ locations (95%+ franchisee-owned = ~2,000-3,000 individual franchisee owners averaging 6-8 units each per IFA data), Subway 20,000+ franchised locations (estimated 20,000-30,000 franchisee owners averaging 2-5 units, many single-unit), 7-Eleven 13,000+ franchised convenience stores, Dunkin' 9,000+ franchised restaurants, Taco Bell, Burger King, Wendy's, Domino's, Papa John's QSR networks, Anytime Fitness 5,000+ franchisee-owned clubs, Planet Fitness, Great Clips 4,400+ salons, Sport Clips, The UPS Store 5,000+ franchised shipping centers, and 100+ other major franchise systems. Target output: 300,000-500,000 individual franchisee owner contact records (deduplicating multi-unit operators who appear across multiple locations, counting each unique owner once with total unit count aggregated), with high-value segment of 50,000-100,000 multi-unit operators owning 5-50 locations each representing 70-80% of total franchise system revenue per International Franchise Association data. Concentrated in QSR/fast casual (burgers, pizza, sandwiches, coffee, chicken, Mexican, Asian), fitness franchises (gyms, boutique fitness studios, yoga/Pilates), automotive services (oil change, transmission, brakes, detailing), personal services (hair salons, massage, tanning, nail salons), home services (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, pest control, cleaning, moving, handyman), business services (shipping/printing, staffing, B2B services), education (tutoring, STEM, child development), senior care (in-home care, memory care), and specialty retail (convenience stores, nutrition, pet supplies). Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) POS and restaurant management software vendors (Toast POS $69-$165/month + 2.49% processing = $800-$2,000/month all-in for busy franchise location = $10,000-$24,000/year, Square, Clover $14.95-$799.95/month + 2.3%, Lightspeed, Revel, SpotOn) where multi-unit franchisee running 1-10 locations pays $10,000-$240,000/year generating $80,000-$2,880,000 lifetime value over 8-12 years = two customers deliver 400×-14,000× database ROI; (2) Payroll, HR, benefits software (Gusto $40/month + $6/employee = $70-$340/month for 5-50 employee franchisee = $840-$4,080/year, ADP $2,000-$10,000/year for multi-unit operators, Paychex, Homebase, 7shifts scheduling) where one multi-unit franchisee = 4×-50× ROI annually; (3) Commercial insurance brokers (general liability, property, workers' comp premiums $15K-$150K/year for single-unit, $150K-$1.5M/year for 10-100 unit operators generating $3K-$300K annual commissions at 20%) where multi-unit client = 15×-1,500× ROI; (4) Equipment suppliers and facilities services (commercial refrigeration, POS hardware, kitchen equipment $20K-$100K remodel per location × 5-10 locations = $100K-$1M multi-unit upgrade, HVAC maintenance, signage, cleaning $500-$5K/month per location) where one multi-unit contract = 250×-5,000× ROI. A one-time $149-$199 CSV delivers 99% savings vs. traditional franchise data vendors charging $0.25-$0.75/contact ($12,500-$37,500 for 50K records), with instant download vs. brand-specific list purchases (Subway list sold separately from McDonald's list creating vendor lock-in), providing complete franchisee owner TAM for POS software, payroll/HR platforms, commercial insurance brokers, and equipment/services suppliers.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four buyer segments with strong LTV and confirmed niche commercial demand (4 vendors actively selling franchise owner lists, premium pricing for brand-specific lists confirms buyer willingness-to-pay): (1) POS/restaurant management software: Multi-unit franchisee running 10 QSR locations pays $100,000-$240,000/year for Toast/Clover POS across all units (mission-critical — cannot process payments without POS, franchisor-mandated tech upgrades every 5-10 years create replacement cycles, integration with delivery platforms DoorDash/UberEats and loyalty programs locks in usage), generating $800,000-$2,880,000 lifetime value over 8-12 year retention = two multi-unit customers deliver $1.6M-$5.76M total LTV = 8,000×-28,800× database ROI. POS vendors actively prospect franchisees during franchisor-mandated upgrade cycles (e.g., when McDonald's mandates new POS rollout across all locations, Toast/Square/Clover compete for 2,000-3,000 franchisee owner decisions each controlling 5-15 units = $50K-$360K contract per franchisee). Vendors pay premium prices for franchise owner contacts vs. generic restaurant lists because franchise purchasing is centralized (one decision-maker controls 5-10 locations vs. independent restaurants requiring 10 separate sales). (2) Payroll/HR software: Multi-unit operator with 10 locations employing 50-500 total staff pays $8,400-$40,800/year for Gusto or $20,000-$100,000/year for ADP Workforce Now (non-negotiable payroll processing, compliance with multi-state wage/hour laws, workers' comp administration, benefits enrollment create switching costs), generating $84,000-$1,000,000 lifetime value over 10 years = one multi-unit franchisee = 420×-5,000× database cost. Franchisees actively seek payroll solutions when scaling from 1-2 locations (manual processing viable) to 5-10+ locations (enterprise HR system required for efficiency and compliance). (3) Commercial insurance: Multi-unit franchisee with 10 QSR locations pays $150,000-$300,000/year in total premiums (general liability $20K-$150K, property $30K-$200K, workers' comp $50K-$500K, commercial auto $10K-$50K, umbrella $5K-$25K) generating $30,000-$60,000 annual broker commission at 20% = $300,000-$600,000 over 10-year relationship = 1,500×-3,000× ROI. Franchise insurance is specialized vertical (QSR franchises have unique liability profiles vs. generic restaurants, fitness franchises need specialized equipment coverage, automotive franchises require garage liability) creating opportunity for brokers with franchise expertise to command premium commissions by offering franchise package policies. Multi-unit operators consolidate insurance across all locations with one broker for volume discounts. (4) Equipment/facilities services: Multi-unit franchisee remodeling 5 locations pays $100,000-$500,000 for commercial kitchen equipment upgrades ($20K-$100K per location × 5) where one contract = 500×-2,500× database ROI. Franchise equipment purchases are cyclical (franchisor-mandated remodels every 7-10 years per franchise agreement, new unit buildouts, end-of-life equipment replacement) creating predictable buying windows. Commercial vendors (refrigeration, HVAC, kitchen equipment) target multi-unit operators for volume pricing and ongoing maintenance contracts ($2K-$10K/year per location preventive maintenance).
